_: The shared LUN each physical rig is provisioned with, by the rig tag tools/mxfs_rig_tag.sh prints. lun_wwid is the SCSI NAA identifier the nodes read from /sys/block/<disk>/device/wwid (or the multipath map's dm uuid); tests/lib/rig.sh mxfs_dev_resolve refuses any device that does not carry it, whatever path named it. A rig with no entry here resolves nothing until one is added (or MXFS_LUN_WWID names the LUN for one run); that is the fail-closed default, not an oversight. host_image is the file or device on THIS host that backs the LUN (an SCST/LIO fileio backstore), for harnesses that read the platter from the host; it is used only when its envelope fsid equals the LUN's (tests/lib/rig.sh mxfs_host_image, tools/mxfs_host_image.sh). A rig whose LUN no host file backs declares null, and those harnesses ABORT there and read the platter from a node instead.

liovm.note: the RESTARTABLE bench target: LIO on the lab VM test32 (tools/lio_bench_target.sh), one block backstore over that VM's second virtio disk, exported as one iSCSI LUN with explicit ACLs for the two TCP-rig node initiators; the nodes reach it as a second SCSI disk beside the 2/tcp rig's LUN. Stood up 2026-09-22 for the fence-matrix target-restart tranche (tests/target_restart_pr.sh), which the 2/tcp rig's target may never be used for. Select it with MXFS_RIG_TAG=liovm and bind the device by identifier (MXFS_DEV=/dev/disk/by-id/wwn-0x<lun_wwid>); a prep that is not told the device formats the transport's default disk, which is the OTHER rig's LUN.
liovm.lun_wwid_note: LIO derives the NAA identifier from the backstore's VPD unit serial, which tools/lio_bench_target.sh fixes before the LUN is exported, so a teardown and re-setup keeps this identifier; read back from both nodes' /sys/block/sdb/device/wwid 2026-09-22 (vendor LIO-ORG, model mxfsbench, rev 4.0, cache_type 'write back').
liovm.host_image_note: the raw file behind the target VM's second disk, on this host; the target submits its I/O straight to that disk and the VM's disk cache is writeback into this host's page cache, so a host-side read sees what the target has accepted. tests/lib/rig.sh uses it only when its envelope fsid equals the LUN's.
liovm.target_vm_note: the libvirt domain on this host that IS the target host. A harness whose subject is a target-host CRASH (tests/target_restart_pr.sh MODE=host) crashes it with virsh destroy and starts it again, which loses everything the target had not written durably — the measurement the tranche asks for — instead of asking the host to reboot itself cleanly over ssh. The service restart (MODE=service) still goes over ssh to the target host's own restart command, named in the lab secrets store under this tag.
liovm.pr_registration_on_session_loss_note: not yet measured on this target; run tests/pr_session_drop_probe.sh under MXFS_RIG_TAG=liovm and record the class here, as the 2/tcp rig's entry does. Until then a harness that predicts PR state across a session loss ABORTs on this rig, by design.

qnap.restart_forbidden_note: This rig's iSCSI target is not restartable for tests: its service is never restarted and its host is never rebooted, by a script or by hand, and no session asks for either (owner's directive, 2026-09-22). A harness whose subject is the target's behaviour across its own restart (tests/target_restart_pr.sh) reads this field first and ABORTs on it before resolving any credential. That tranche runs against a restartable target declared under its own tag here, without this field.
qnap.note: the 50 GiB QNAP iSCSI LUN of the 2/tcp rig, bound by run.sh as /dev/disk/by-id/wwn-0x6e843b6393a5a6ed918bd4f4fdb8e7d6. Never by /dev/sda: the nodes also see the liovm bench target, and either can enumerate as sda.
qnap.host_image_note: the LUN lives on the QNAP; no file on this host backs it. ~/disk.img is the fileio image of the earlier SCST rig and is NOT this LUN.
qnap.pr_registration_on_session_loss_evidence: QNAP TS-453 Pro iSCSI target, one session per node, no multipath. Measured 2026-09-04 by tests/pr_session_drop_probe.sh (tests/evidence/prsd_s501a.log, prsd_s501b.log): a virsh-destroyed node's registration is gone from READ KEYS within ~34 s of the power cut with the PR generation UNCHANGED (a target-internal purge, no PROUT). Re-measured 2026-09-19 by tests/fence_crash_cuts.sh sweep s71a (tests/evidence/20260919T165654Z_fcut1_s71a-c1/K0.txt K1.txt K2.txt): two keys before the destroy, one from the survivor parked before any fence intent, zero after both hosts were destroyed with no MXFS instance alive. Re-run the probe when the target, its firmware or the session topology changes. tests/lib/rig.sh mxfs_rig_pr_class reads this; a harness that predicts PR state ABORTs on a rig that declares none.
qnap.task_retirement_on_nexus_loss_evidence: MEASURED 2026-09-20 by tests/pr_retirement_probe.sh (tests/evidence/20260920T002025Z_prret_s75t, console tests/evidence/prret_s75t.console): with no module loaded, the victim ran 32 O_DIRECT threads writing rising counters into 32 blocks at the end of the LUN and the survivor read that window in a tight loop, logging every change. The writer was confirmed reaching the platter (383 change rows, counter 14180 at the stop). The victim was then POWER-CUT with virsh destroy, not shut down, so whatever it had submitted was left in the target's queue with nobody to answer to. The window went quiescent at the cut and NEVER CHANGED AGAIN for the remaining 160.3 s: LATE_ROWS=0. The registration purge arrived between 30 s and 46 s after the cut (READ KEYS 2,2,1,1,...), i.e. about 26 s AFTER the platter had already gone quiet - so on this target the task-retirement boundary PRECEDES the registration purge that the boot-succession fence keys on, rather than following it. WHAT THIS DOES NOT SAY: it is a qualified contract for THIS target, firmware, backend and session topology and may never be promoted into a promise about arbitrary SPC targets (design ruling, docs/rulings/fence-ambiguous-drain-and-proof-resume.md). Its resolution is bounded by the observer's 50 ms change-row rate limit, so it excludes a late landing more than ~50 ms after the cut, not one within it. It covers NEXUS LOSS only - not a registration removed by a PREEMPT AND ABORT while the victim's session stays up, and not a voluntary REGISTER-with-zero, neither of which retires anything by itself. Re-run the probe when the target, its firmware or the session topology changes.
qnap.task_retirement_contract_withdrawn_why: WITHDRAWN 0.89.16, and withdrawn in code rather than by deleting this line: the module no longer accepts ANY deployment clause as a retirement basis, so this rig ships no contract and setting one changes no outcome (it is reported as rejected in the refusal).  The string this rig used to The string is kept verbatim in task_retirement_contract_withdrawn so the harness can load a module WITH it and prove the refusal is in code rather than in configuration.  WHY IT WENT: a clause is a conditional whose premise no initiator can establish, and its entire support was four laps of tests/pr_retirement_probe.sh that saw no late write inside a 180 s window sampled at 50 ms.  That characterises this appliance under one workload; it cannot exclude a command the target retained without it ever becoming observable, and nothing in the module can detect a target that breaks the assertion.  A certificate minted on it authorises replaying a foreign journal slice, where a surviving accepted write lands as an unordered logical write into metadata the replay is rewriting - silent corruption, against a refusal that only costs availability.  Design ruling: docs/rulings/retirement-witness-routes-lu-reset-early-preempt-or-refuse.md.  THE MEASUREMENTS ARE KEPT BELOW as observations of this target, because they are true and because re-measuring them is how a future witnessed mechanism gets characterised - they are not, and never were, a guarantee.
qnap.task_retirement_contract_withdrawn_obser: THE DEPLOYMENT ASSERTION the running module requires before it will certify a boot succession (dlm/scsipr.h mxfs_scsipr_retire_basis_nexus_loss; module parameter target_retire_contract, shipped by run.sh and tests/setup/prep_node.sh). Five fields: the T10 vendor, product and REVISION the LUN reports through INQUIRY, the designator from its device identification VPD page, and the clause asserted. Read from test1 2026-09-20: vendor 'QNAP', product 'iSCSI Storage', revision '4.0', wwid naa.6e843b6393a5a6ed918bd4f4fdb8e7d6 (/sys/block/sda/device/{vendor,model,rev,wwid}). The revision is in the contract deliberately: a firmware upgrade stops the module matching, so the qualification has to be re-measured rather than silently inherited. WHAT BACKS THIS ASSERTION, stated plainly because it is NOT a witness: FOUR laps of tests/pr_retirement_probe.sh on this LUN - s75t nslot=32 (tests/evidence/20260920T002025Z_prret_s75t), s76r1 nslot=32 (20260920T012019Z_prret_s76r1), s76r3 nslot=16 (20260920T012351Z_prret_s76r3) and s80r4 nslot=64 (20260920T021228Z_prret_s80r4). Each power-cut a node writing rising O_DIRECT counters into the LUN tail while the survivor read that window in a tight loop; each saw the window go quiescent at the cut with LATE_ROWS=0 and no change for the remaining ~160 s, and READ KEYS showed the registration purge arriving tens of seconds AFTER that quiescence. A fifth attempt (s76r2 nslot=64) ABORTED at stage=capture without measuring anything - the victim was still booting from the previous lap ('No route to host') - which is the probe refusing rather than guessing. WHAT THAT IS AND IS NOT: it is OBSERVED BEHAVIOUR under these workloads and a 180 s observation window with a 50 ms change-row rate limit. It cannot exclude a retained command that never became observable in that window, the reads see logical contents (possibly through target cache) rather than the platter, and more laps improve characterisation without turning absence of observed late writes into an assured ordering guarantee. It is not a vendor contract. The module cannot detect a target that violates the assertion; what it can do, and now does, is refuse to certify where no assertion has been made at all. THE CLAUSE WAS REWORDED 2026-09-20 (0.89.15) AND THIS RIG RE-ASSERTS IT DELIBERATELY. The old clause, nexus-loss-retires-before-registration-purge, is conditional on a NEXUS LOSS that no initiator can witness - the target never reports why a registration left its table - so matching it established that the deployment had made an assertion while its premise was never established for the fence in hand (design ruling, docs/rulings/retirement-proof-obligation-and-observed-transition-classes.md). The clause now asserted is about the transition an initiator CAN state: when a registration disappears from this LUN's table AND MXFS issued no replacement for it, every command the target had accepted on that registration's nexus has completed or aborted with its effects ordered before the disappearance. WHAT THAT ADDS TO WHAT WAS MEASURED: the four probe laps above are all power cuts, i.e. nexus losses with no MXFS replacement, which is exactly the covered case; the clause additionally requires that NO AGENT OUTSIDE THIS CLUSTER issues persistent-reservation commands against this LUN, since an administrative PREEMPT or CLEAR would remove a registration without retiring anything. That is true of this rig by provisioning - the LUN is reached only by the two test nodes and this repository's own harnesses - and it is asserted here rather than assumed silently. The module now refuses the two transitions this measurement does not cover: a key one of our own mounts replaced, whether from the same boot or a later one. The old clause is still recognised by the module and always refused, with that reason printed, so a deployment carrying it finds out rather than being certified from a premise nobody established.
qnap.preempt_abort_absent_sark_evidence: MEASURED 2026-09-20 by tests/pr_absent_sark_probe.sh lap s89a (tests/evidence/20260920T192919Z_prabs_s89a/summary.txt). On an idle cluster with no mxfs mount, test1 registered 0x5a5a0a01, test2 registered 0x5a5a0b01 and test1 reserved Write Exclusive - All Registrants (type 7), which is the reservation the module holds. Three PREEMPT AND ABORT commands were then issued from test1 with rk=0x5a5a0a01 and prout-type=7, differing only in the service-action key. ARM A, sark=0x5a5a0f01 which was never registered anywhere: RESERVATION CONFLICT (sg_persist rc=24), both registrations still present, PR generation 0x175e -> 0x175e. ARM B, sark=0x5a5a0b01 after test2 removed it, i.e. a key that WAS in the table and left - the transition the ordinary fence races: RESERVATION CONFLICT (rc=24), the remaining registration untouched, PR generation 0x175e -> 0x175e. ARM C, the control, same command with sark=0x5a5a0b01 re-registered: ACCEPTED (rc=0), the named registration removed, PR generation 0x175f -> 0x1760. The control is what makes A and B mean anything: the command shape, the reservation key, the type and the apparatus can produce an acceptance in the same lap, so the two refusals are about the absent key and nothing else. WHAT THIS ESTABLISHES: on this LUN the target evaluates the service-action key at scope selection and refuses when it matches no registration, so a PREEMPT AND ABORT that raced the victim's departure is distinguished from one that covered it by the target's own status - it is unreachable as a silent success, not merely unwitnessed. The module already depends on exactly this: pal/linux/kern.c mxfs_pal_scsi_pr_preempt turns status 0x18 into -EBUSY, dlm/scsipr.c scsipr_preempt_locked logs it as 'key not registered; no registration removed and no task set aborted by us', and mxfs_scsipr_fence_node classifies it MXFS_FENCE_KIND_RACE_LOST, which carries no retirement claim. WHAT IT DOES NOT SAY: it is a qualified observation of THIS target, firmware revision and session topology and may never be promoted into a promise about arbitrary SPC targets. It also says nothing about a registration removed DURING the command's execution, which no initiator can schedule. Re-run the probe when the target, its firmware or the session topology changes.

scst-fio.note: clyde's own SCST iSCSI target (scripts/scst_setup.sh): vdisk_fileio device 'mxfs' over ~/disk.img, target iqn.2026-05.local.mxfs:shared on portal 192.168.120.1, reached by in-guest iSCSI (run.sh condition cawd, the default device /dev/disk/by-path/ip-192.168.120.1:3260-iscsi-iqn.2026-05.local.mxfs:shared-lun-0). SCST implements COMPARE AND WRITE and persistent reservations. Since 2026-09-26 it is the shared LUN of the 2-node rig (test1/test2) and of the four platform verification pairs (the lab file's storage line), replacing the retired QNAP.
scst-fio.lun_wwid_note: read back from test1's /sys/block/sda/device/wwid 2026-09-26 (vendor SCST_FIO, by-id scsi-SSCST_FIO_mxfs_2e476d07). SCST derives it from the device name, so a teardown and re-setup of device 'mxfs' keeps it.
scst-fio.host_image_note: the vdisk_fileio backing file on this host, opened o_direct by the target, so a host-side read sees what the target has written. tests/lib/rig.sh uses it only when its envelope fsid equals the LUN's.
scst-fio.pr_registration_on_session_loss_evidence: MEASURED 2026-09-26 by tests/pr_session_drop_probe.sh prsd_scst_s6a (tests/evidence/20260926T155819Z_prsd_prsd_scst_s6a, console tests/evidence/prsd_scst_s6a.console), both nodes mounted on 2-node CAW: test2 was power-cut with virsh destroy at 15:58:25Z. The registration count stayed 2 until +64 s, when it fell to 1 with the PR generation MOVING (0xa -> 0xb) - a PROUT, not a target-internal purge: test1's own kernel log at that instant reads 'P-PR-FENCE preempt-and-aborted dead node 338711679 (key 0xe292b6bf50a30e79) ... gen=11: EXCLUSION PROVED' and 'P236-FENCE-CERTIFIED ... kind=PREEMPT_ABORT_PROVEN_V1', i.e. MXFS's survivor fenced the still-present key once the heartbeat dead window (~62 s) expired. So the target kept the dead initiator's registration for the whole window and the exact-key PREEMPT AND ABORT found it. After the victim booted and logged in again (no mxfs mount) its login added no registration and its WRITE to LBA 131087 was refused with RESERVATION CONFLICT under the held Write Exclusive - All Registrants reservation. The probe's own line 'registration count dropped after the kill without any PROUT' means no PROUT issued by the probe; the generation move is the survivor's fence. Re-run the probe when the SCST build, its configuration or the session topology changes.
